transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alicia Park, Samir Patel (Redwood); Maya Chen, Diego Ruiz, Emma Li (NovaFinance)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize and how batching + KV/prefix caching can reduce per-token cost for NovaFinance workload; tradeoffs on latency and hit rate assumptions; plan to run pilot.

[00:00] Alicia Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh, I'm Alicia, I'm the AE on this deal, and with me is Samir from our SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya Chen: all good, thanks. excited to see the Optimize walkthrough — we've been poking at the docs but want to understand real config impacts.
[00:12] Diego Ruiz: yeah, mostly interested in latency numbers and like, how caching would work with our session state.
[00:18] Samir Patel: great. quick agenda: we'll show the Optimize UI, run through batching recommendations, then prefix/KV cache behavior and the cost model. i'll flag where assumptions live in the sheet.
[00:26] Emma Li: sounds good. also want to confirm security questions later — SSO, KMS, audit logs.
[00:32] Alicia Park: yep we'll cover that briefly and then follow up with the full security pack.

[02:05] Samir Patel: okay jumping in — here's the Optimize console, on the left you can see per-route token breakdown, observed latencies, and the suggested batch settings. so for NovaFinance traffic pattern you told us you have lots of short queries with high QPS and some long-form summarization spikes, right?
[02:20] Maya Chen: yep that's right, mostly short queries during market hours and batch reconciliation jobs overnight that are longer.
[02:28] Samir Patel: perfect — so recommendation is two-tiered: small immediate batches for interactive flows (target batch size 1-8, max wait 15ms) to keep p95 latency tight, and a background larger batching profile for non-interactive jobs (batch size 16-64). that gives you good throughput without pushing the interactive latency too high.
[02:45] Diego Ruiz: can you explain the "max wait" param — is that queue time before dispatch?
[02:49] Samir Patel: exactly, it's the max latency we allow to collect more requests into a batch. we set it at 15ms for interactive to avoid user-visible lag; for nightly jobs you can set 50-200ms and favor throughput.

[05:10] Samir Patel: on to KV/prefix cache — prefix cache is essentially storing the KV cache for completed prefixes so subsequent requests with the same prefix avoid re-computation. in our console you set expected hit-rate and TTL, and Optimize will show estimated token savings and cost delta.
[05:25] Maya Chen: what's a realistic hit-rate for our type of conversational QA across customers?
[05:29] Samir Patel: depends, but for templated prompts and consistent prefixes we often see 30-60% hit rates; for highly personalized sessions it's lower. for NovaFinance where many prompts start with common compliance/legal boilerplate, assume 35-45% initially.
[05:40] Alicia Park: and that assumption feeds straight into the cost model — the spreadsheet we shared earlier has the math.

[07:00] Diego Ruiz: how do we handle privacy — we can't store PII in cache, right?
[07:05] Samir Patel: correct, you mask or strip PII upstream. Redwood supports per-route cache controls and can disable prefix cache for sensitive routes. plus with Private deployments you can keep caches on customer-managed storage.

[09:15] Samir Patel: jumping to cost model: Optimize shows per-token compute cost (in $), estimated tokens saved by cache, and net savings after added storage/eviction overhead. example: with 40% cache hit, average prompt 60 tokens, we estimate ~24 tokens saved per request for those that hit, giving an effective token reduction of about 9.6 tokens per request across all traffic.
[09:34] Emma Li: can you show the numbers? like, translate to dollars per 100k requests?
[09:40] Samir Patel: sure — if your hosted rate is $0.0004 per token compute (illustrative), 9.6 tokens saved => $0.00384 saved per request, so at 100k requests that's ~$384 saved. then subtract small storage costs — our model uses S3 class cold-tier rates, for typical TTLs the storage add is under $50/month at that scale.
[10:05] Maya Chen: okay that's a helpful ballpark. how sensitive is the model to hit rate assumptions?
[10:12] Samir Patel: pretty sensitive; a 10pp drop in hit-rate drops savings proportionally. Optimize has a slider that recalculates savings live. we recommend pilot runs to measure empirical hit rate before committing to dedicated configs.

[12:40] Alicia Park: question from the deck — dedicated vs hosted: if NovaFinance wants guaranteed p95 latency and throughput during market open, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is recommended. hosted still works but you'd want burst policies and routing to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[12:55] Diego Ruiz: what about cost delta for dedicated? we run 24/7 during market hours and need low jitter.
[13:02] Samir Patel: dedicated has fixed reserved cost but predictable per-hour; you buy Reserved vCPU/GPU capacity. we'll model it in the pilot pricing — sometimes combined approach (hosted for burst, dedicated for baseline) is most cost efficient.

[15:30] Samir Patel: a couple of practical suggestions from Optimize: 1) prefix cache TTL: start with 12 hours for market-day patterns and 72 hours for overnight batch common prefixes; tune based on eviction rates. 2) aim for small batch sizes for interactive flows and aggressively cache repeated prefixes. 3) enable continuous batching in the runtime so we can safely lower max wait without sacrificing throughput.
[15:52] Maya Chen: will enabling continuous batching increase latency variability?
[15:55] Samir Patel: not if configured correctly; continuous batching just opportunistically piggybacks on in-flight requests. we show distribution plots in the Console to pick safe thresholds.

[18:20] Alicia Park: note on quantization — if you use int8/backing quantized variants that reduces compute per-token and often changes the sweet spot for batching; Optimize will recommend quant profiles per-model.
[18:32] Diego Ruiz: do you automatically switch quantized variants in-flight?
[18:35] Samir Patel: we support model variants and smart routing; infra can fallback to a quantized variant when capacity's tight, but we recommend A/B testing for quality regressions.

[22:00] Emma Li: what data do you need from us to run a trial?
[22:05] Samir Patel: QPS traces, sample prompts, a few representative conversation sessions, and SLO targets (p95 latency target). that's it to produce a realistic cost/latency simulation.
[22:15] Maya Chen: we'll share those — Diego will pull logs and sanitize them.

[25:00] Diego Ruiz: quick nit — in the cost model sheet there was a line called "KV cache write amplification" — what is that?
[25:05] Samir Patel: yeah that accounts for extra writes when you update keys frequently; for instance if your sessions constantly mutate the prefix then eviction churn causes more storage/API ops. we model it as a multiplier on storage and small extra compute. set it conservatively to 1.1–1.5 depending on churn.

[28:40] Samir Patel: also important: network egress and inter-region routing can change effective latency; Optimize's region-aware model factors in regional price differences and additional latency overheads.

[31:20] Alicia Park: are there any blocking security requirements on your side before a pilot?
[31:25] Emma Li: we need SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and audit logs retention policy — ideally SSO + KMS before any production movement.
[31:34] Alicia Park: we have those. i'll share the security packet post-call.

[35:10] Samir Patel: demo time — i'm going to switch to the benchmark tab and run a short simulated run using a 10-minute sample of NovaFinance patterns (this is synthetic in the console). watch the charts — you'll see p50/p95 change as we change batch/window settings.
[35:25] Diego Ruiz: looks like p95 jumps when you increase batch windows beyond 40ms for interactive.
[35:29] Samir Patel: yes, that's expected — it's a tail behavior. the console also shows per-route tradeoffs so you can tune per-route max wait.

[38:45] Maya Chen: ok, recap?
[38:48] Alicia Park: recap: 1) SE will run a tailored latency/cost model with NovaFinance traces and propose concrete batch size and cache TTLs; 2) AE to send pilot pricing and security pack; 3) Customer to provide QPS traces and sample prompts; 4) schedule a 1-week joint benchmark after initial config.
[39:10] Emma Li: agreeable. one more ask — can you include recommended monitoring dashboards for cache hit rate and eviction metrics?
[39:17] Samir Patel: yes will include a dashboard template and alert thresholds.

[42:00] Diego Ruiz: thanks, this was useful. small comment: in the transcript deck you called our nightly job "reconciliation spikes" which is accurate.
[42:08] Alicia Park: thanks Diego. we'll follow up with the deliverables.

[44:30] Alicia Park: ok closing — thanks everyone, we'll send materials and next steps.
[44:36] Maya Chen: thanks all.

References: shared deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/optimize-pilot.pdf), cost spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/sheets/novafinance-cost-model), security packet placeholder (link: https://redwood.ai/security/packet).
